title: Mission: The Anemometer
subtitle: Catch the wind
summary: Discover how moving air turns an anemometer and compare gentle and strong wind.
activityInstruction: Predict which wind makes the cups spin fastest. Test calm, gentle and strong wind, record each observation, then compare.

storyQuestions.success: The children went to the park.

storyQuestions.prompt: What did they go there for?
storyQuestions.success: They went to the park for a picnic.

storyQuestions.prompt: What was the weather like at first?
storyQuestions.success: At first the weather was sunny.
Their hair blew in the wind.
The wind made the napkin fly.

storyQuestions.prompt: Was the wind strong or gentle at first?
storyQuestions.success: At first the wind was strong.

storyQuestions.prompt: What happened to the wind later?
What do we call moving air?
Can we see the wind itself?
storyQuestions.success: No, we cannot see the wind itself.

storyQuestions.prompt: Can we see things move in the wind?
storyQuestions.success: Yes, we can see things move in the wind.

storyQuestions.prompt: What might the wind make our model do?
storyQuestions.success: The wind might make our model spin.

storyQuestions.prompt: What might happen when the wind gets stronger?
storyQuestions.success: When the wind gets stronger, our model spins faster.

parts.label: Cups
parts.fact: The wind pushes the cups and makes the rotor turn.
parts.help: Find the three curved cups around the top.

parts.label: Arms
parts.fact: The arms hold the cups away from the shaft and turn with them.
parts.help: Find the three bars joining the cups to the centre.

parts.label: Shaft
parts.fact: The rotor turns around the upright shaft.
parts.help: Find the upright pole beneath the cups.

parts.label: Wind vane
parts.fact: The wind vane points into the wind and shows where the wind comes from. The cups measure wind speed.
parts.help: Find the arrow below the cups.

exploreInstruction: Change the wind. Watch the cups and arms turn around the shaft. Faster spinning means stronger wind; this model does not give a calibrated wind speed.
codingInstruction: Plan a wind experiment: choose a setting, observe, record and repeat. Coding instructions for the classroom hardware can be added here.
